    **11+. City-states as powers** (moved forward on 21 October 2026). City-states become powers like the kings: the same rules, envoys and characters, and the same goal on one scoreboard ("One scoreboard for every power" under Victory). It comes here, after item 11, because some twenty courts writing letters need real carriers, which 11b brings, and the wealth of a realm from 9+a; and it comes this early because most of the Amarna letters are vassals' letters, so a game tested only on the great kings writing to each other is a different game from the one the letters describe ("The Levant, the boiling pot" under The world). Design the scoreboard first, here, since every script player optimises what it rewards: par for each starting position, tribute included, and how the land weighs against gold and goods in a realm's wealth ("The wealth of a realm" under Victory), with tribute scoring itself as wealth that crosses a border ("What a breach means, and to whom"); check whether kings build vassal networks as well as conquer, and win rates per power. Then vassalage in words, with the marked vassal tablet and its structured-press template ("Vassalage is words"); cities starting in the relation they historically had ("Opening relations as they were"); and minds that follow what is at stake ("Minds follow what is at stake"). Today's purchase of a city goes: a city comes under another's power by agreement or by conquest. Script city-states play by the same expected-growth logic as script kings ("Every feature is every seat's"). Depends on items 5 and 7 too, since vassals react to news as it arrives and bargain behind walls. Recount the pool here and set each power's starting staff ("How many characters"). The game also ends when only one power is left ("When one power is left" under Victory). For the opening relations, the builder starts from the table under "Opening relations as they were". Each court also gets its state of the realm at the start ("A state of the realm" under The world). The ways cities become free, which need governors and commanders, come in item 17. **Stop for review.**
